To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LOXL2 selective inhibitors reduce cross-links in the ECM and alter matrix properties of a model of fibroblast foci in IPF.

“We developed a novel in vitro fibroblast foci model and showed that the small molecule LOXL2 inhibitors, BMS-986094 and BMS-986095, reduced collagen cross-linking in the fibroblast focs and altered the mechanical properties of the fibrotic ECM.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new, small molecule inhibitors that target the LOXL2 enzyme.
the role of LOX in the pathogenesis of pulmonary fibrosis, and we are investigating the potential therapeutic effects of selective LOX inhibitors.
the development of a novel in vitro 3D model of fibroblast foci (Jones and colleagues AJRCCM, 2015) that recapitulates key features of IPF lung tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LOXL2 inhibitor 1,3,4,8-tetramethyl-5H-imidazo[1,2-a] pyrazine-6,7-dione (TMIP) inhibits the LOXL2 activity, but not the LOX activity.
the use of a small molecule inhibitor of LOXL2 is a promising approach for the treatment of IPF.

the results of the current meta-analysis indicate a significant association between the LOXL2 rs3825942 polymorphism and the risk of gastric cancer, especially in the East Asian population, which is consistent with the results of a previous study [ 23 ].
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LOX inhibition reduces fibroblastic focus formation, and this is associated with a reduction in cross-linking and a change in matrix properties, and that these effects are selective to LOXL2.
we are developing a new model system that is based upon the formation of fibroblasts foci in IPF.
we have developed a novel model of fibroblast foci that recapitulates the key features of the disease, including a high level of LOX expression and activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LOXL2 inhibitor, BMS-986094, has a unique profile in that it is able to reduce the formation of cross-links and also reduce the amount of collagen in an in vitro model of lung fibrosis.
LOXL2 is the most likely LOX to be involved in the formation of collagen cross-links.
the small molecule inhibitors of LOXL2 we identified have the potential to reduce the cross-linking of collagen, and therefore the stiffness, of the matrix.
